predecessors.name: Emirate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: the Vic country, Cardona and Casserès, taken from al-Andalus from 798

successors.name: County of Barcelona
successors.text: Osona, which 'returned to Barcelona' when Jimena and Bernard died without heirs

ledger.x: 798: Louis of Aquitaine sets Borrell to rebuild Vic, Cardona and Casserès, and the county begins.
801: Borrell is made Count of Osona.
826: Guillemó and Aissó take Osona in their rebellion.
879: Wilfred the Hairy begins the repopulation of Osona.
879: Osona is held by the counts of Barcelona.
990: the pagus of Berga leaves Osona.
1003: the western third of the shape is gone in Cliopatria.
1035: Guisla de Lluçà and her son William rule Osona.
1040: Osona is 'augmented by the addition of the County of Manresa, which was subsumed within Osona'.
1054: Osona returns to the counts of Barcelona; the year is the list's.
1056: Cliopatria's shape drops back to the 1003 outline.
1107: Osona goes to the Count of Besalú.
1111: Osona becomes a permanent part of Catalonia.
1111: the County of Osona ends; 'The "county" and "count" of Osona disappeared as distinct terms after 1107-1111.'

wars.name: Revolt of Aissó and Guillemó
wars.outcome: 'After the rebellion of 826, during which Guillemó and Aissó succeeded in taking it with help from the Emirate of Córdoba'; Osona then 'remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'.

wars.name: Almanzor's sack of Barcelona (985)
wars.outcome: 'In 985 Barcelona, then ruled by Borrell II, was attacked and burned by Muslims, led by Almanzor'; the count took refuge in the Montserrat mountains.

certainty.note: County lands defined by castles and pagi (Vic, Cardona, Casserès, Berga, Manresa); no treaty or survey line on any page opened.
